threads.body: [General] This fallback also matches ZGC, whose collector names are not handled by the switch. When `jvm.gc.duration` is selected for JFR, `RuntimeTelemetryBuilder` disables its JMX collection, so the existing ZGC pause-duration series disappear: generic collection events measure whole cycles, not individual pauses, even with `requireCompleteJmxReplacement=true`. Restrict the fallback to the native-image collectors so other collectors retain their JMX metrics.

replies.body:
Good catch. ZGC and Shenandoah had no handler in the switch, so `jvm.gc.duration` stayed on JMX for them, and the fallback would have replaced the pause durations with whole cycles.

Fixed in 97521e4. The fallback now also requires that the JVM registers none of the collector-specific event types: `jdk.G1GarbageCollection`, `jdk.YoungGarbageCollection` and `jdk.OldGarbageCollection`. HotSpot registers them for every collector, so ZGC and Shenandoah keep their JMX metrics. A GraalVM native image registers only the generic event, so it still gets the fallback. A test covers ZGC with all event types present.

threads.body: I think this isn't needed since gc events aren't periodic

replies.body: Right, removed. I had copied it from the G1, young and old collection handlers, which set the same period.

No, because of ZGC and Shenandoah. HotSpot registers `jdk.G1GarbageCollection`, `jdk.YoungGarbageCollection` and `jdk.OldGarbageCollection` for every collector. I checked this on JDK 21 and 25 with ZGC, Shenandoah and G1. The collector names match no case of the switch, so `handlers` stays empty. Examples are `ZGC Pauses` and `ZGC Cycles` on 21, or `ZGC Minor Pauses` on 25.

With `handlers.isEmpty()` alone, a ZGC application that selects `jvm.gc.duration` for JFR would get the generic handler. `RuntimeTelemetryBuilder` then drops `jvm.gc.duration` from JMX, because JFR provides it. Whole-collection durations would then replace the JMX series with separate pauses and cycles. The extra check keeps the fallback for the native image case, where none of the specific event types exists.

threads.body: usually we add `// visible for testing` for method that aren't private only because they are used from tests

The [README](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/f01d8e617392e13fd33840c4d3605b4b2e121c49/instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/library/README.md#L218) says JFR duration points include `jvm.gc.action`, but the library omits it when it reads the generic GC event used by GraalVM Native Image:

```diff
diff --git a/instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/library/README.md b/instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/library/README.md
--- a/instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/library/README.md
+++ b/instrumentation/runtime-telemetry/library/README.md
@@ -217,4 +217,6 @@
 
-Every JMX-sourced `jvm.gc.duration` point also includes `jvm.gc.cause`, omitted from the examples below because its value varies by collection (for example, `Allocation Failure` or `System.gc()`). When selected for JFR on Java 17+, `jvm.gc.duration` points include only `jvm.gc.name` and `jvm.gc.action`, not `jvm.gc.cause`.
+Every JMX-sourced `jvm.gc.duration` point also includes `jvm.gc.cause`, omitted from the examples below because its value varies by collection (for example, `Allocation Failure` or `System.gc()`).
+
+On Java 17+, JFR-sourced `jvm.gc.duration` points include `jvm.gc.name` but not `jvm.gc.cause`. They also include `jvm.gc.action` unless they come from the generic `jdk.GarbageCollection` event. GraalVM Native Image's serial collector emits this event without identifying the collection as young or full.
 
 - CMS Garbage Collector
```

threads.body: [Simplification] This leaves three `getHandlers` overloads, each passing one more input to the next. Only one test, `doesNotCreateInstrumentsForUnavailableEvents`, calls the five-argument version. Move the GC-name collection into the four-argument overload, alongside the JFR event-name discovery, and call the six-argument overload directly from there. Then delete this overload and have that test pass `emptySet(), List.of()`. That leaves two steps: discover the runtime inputs, then pick handlers from explicit inputs.

replies.body: Applied in 18bc87bdbf: the four-argument overload now collects both the JFR event names and the collector names, and the test passes `emptySet(), List.of()`.

threads.body:
```suggestion
On Java 17+, JFR-sourced `jvm.gc.duration` points include `jvm.gc.name` but not `jvm.gc.cause`. They also include `jvm.gc.action` unless they come from the generic `jdk.GarbageCollection` event. GraalVM Native Image's serial collector emits this event without identifying the collection as young or full.

To collect `jvm.gc.duration` with GraalVM Native Image's Serial GC, build the image with
`--enable-monitoring=jfr` and include `jvm.gc.duration` in the JFR metric selector.
```
